title: Seawall Week of 8-24 — Campaign Report
sub: MRU91 · 2026-08-25 → 08-28 · standard post-process pipeline: per-day reports from the two canonical modules, stitched into this rollup
rollup_html:
The week in one arc

The week reads as one arc: fix the pointing, then fight the association. 8/25 proved the −2.2° azimuth bias made the target untrackable everywhere it flew. The overnight yaw-offset fix landed; 8/26 measured the −1.45° residual and showed the radar is a 22–27 m sensor once that is corrected — while tracks fragmented (12 ids/flight) against continuous detections. 8/27 moved to engagements and exposed the close-pass regime: error inflating exactly at endgame, one guidance dash flown inside a track handover gap, and no target track during the killing dive. 8/28 delivered the week's engagements — 21 m and 32 m ×2 at up to 99.8% coverage with the cal holding below the 1° reporting bar — and matured the close-pass problem into identity corruption: three track steals at the crossings.

days.title: 8/25 — Tracking (2 flights)
days.notes_html: Key message: the pre-cal −2.2° azimuth bias dominated everything. The target drone (mav14550) was never tracked at all — 0 target-side tracks, all day, everywhere it flew — so the panes below follow the second drone (mav14551_2_2), the only aircraft the radar held: 33–54% coverage, 92–116 m errors that are almost entirely the azimuth bias projected at range. The tracker also sat idle until 14:39. This day is the why for the overnight yaw-offset fix.
days.key_message_html: Pre-cal az bias −2.2° dominated — target drone never tracked; panes follow the only tracked drone

days.title: 8/26 — Tracking (2 flights × 2 laps)
days.notes_html: Key message: cal applied — the residual azimuth bias is measured, small, and explains most of the remaining error. Post-cal az −1.45° (el +0.5°, alt +21 m). Raw 65–68 m horizontal error collapses to 22–27 m with the residual corrected offline — accuracy is calibration-limited, not sensor-limited. Continuity is the other story: 12 track ids per flight and 6 turn handovers against continuous ~2 det/s — association-limited, the thread that runs through the engagement days.
days.key_message_html: Cal applied — residual az −1.45° measured; 22–27 m corrected; continuity association-limited

One guidance dash this engagement was flown entirely inside the 454→633 track handover gap, and track error inflated right at endgame (a ~70 m pass read as 34 m; altitude ran away +280 m).

engagements.summary_html: The radar was blind through the dive: the target's MAVLink truth was frozen, and the only target track (1124) initiated 13 s after the dive bottom, 3.6 km out — too late to appear in the standard t−10…t+5 CPA window below. Target truth here is the target's onboard GPS log; the 39 m CPA is GPS-to-GPS. Closest approach vs the late radar track (searched ±120 s): {cpa_track:.0f} m.

radar_rollup.intro_html: Every radar issue the campaign surfaced, in one place. Narrative sections are the day-report findings; the turn statistics and the heat map are computed from the archived data at build time.
radar_rollup.az_bias_html:
The dominant error source of the week, measured independently every day at both the raw-observation and track level. The yaw-offset fix landed overnight 8/25→8/26; after that the residual stayed under the 1° reporting bar and holds through redeploys.

dayazimuth biasstate
8/25−2.2°pre-cal — target drone untrackable everywhere it flew; at 3 km a 2.2° bias is a 115 m cross-range offset
8/26−1.45°post-fix residual; raw 65–68 m horizontal error collapses to 22–27 m with the residual corrected offline — accuracy is calibration-limited, not sensor-limited
8/27−0.19°cal holding (phase-1 measurement)
8/28−0.21° / −0.45°live / recomputed — still under the reporting bar through the overnight redeploy
radar_rollup.turns_html: Tracks are held on the straights and lost in the racetrack turns: detections stay continuous (~2/s) while association breaks as the target maneuvers, so tracks coast, go tentative, and hand over. 8/26 logged 12 track ids per flight with the handovers clustered at the turn ends, and the turn penalty is 1.7–1.9× on 8/26–8/27. On 8/28 the ratio inverts (0.8×) — not because turns got better, but because the dominant holes that day sit on the STRAIGHT low-altitude eastern leg (the corridor in the heat map below), which outweighs the turn losses.
radar_rollup.steals_html: The close-pass failure mode matured over the week: on 8/27 the errors inflated at endgame (a ~70 m pass read as 34 m), one guidance dash was flown entirely inside the 454→633 track handover gap, and there was no target track at all during the dive. On 8/28, with 23 scoreable passes, coverage was no longer the problem — a track always reacquired — but IDENTITY was: 3 track steals. Track 177 was stolen by the interceptor after pass 3 (Flight 1); track 1551, born on the interceptor, was stolen by the target at pass 6 (Flight 4); plus one drag-and-die (129). Track error at the pass is comparable to the miss distance itself, so radar-only endgame scoring is ±1 pass-width.
radar_rollup.heatmap_html: Where tracks go bad around the flight pattern: per 30 m cell (so the grid follows the actual truth line), the percentage of moving-target time with an ACTIVE track (confirmed and measurement-updated within ±0.75 s), combined over the scoreable days (8/26–8/28) on real terrain. Cells are colored by the percentile of percent-active across all cells — the bottom 15% of cells clamp to solid red — because most cells are near-perfect and a raw linear scale washes the structure out; hover any cell for its true active %. The recurring weak pocket is the low-altitude eastern leg (E +1.0–2.0 km) — line-of-sight, not range. 8/25 is excluded: zero target-side tracks all day under the pre-cal bias.

radar_rollup.corruption_html: Distinct from a steal: the track keeps the right identity but its STATE goes bad exactly at the crossing — error inflates at endgame, so radar-only miss scoring is ±1 pass-width. The clearest case: run 214a1a56 (Ivory_Rattlesnake), 8/27 Engagement 1, trk 633 at 09:51:28 PDT — a 72 m truth-truth pass that the track read as 44 m, with the elevation/altitude excursion right at CPA visible below. The same signature repeats on run e65bd4f9 (8/28): at Flight 4's 32 m passes the track error (59–67 m) exceeds the miss itself.
